title.en: Middle East crisis live: Rubio hopes US can reach Hormuz deal with Iran ‘very shortly’ as officials say progress has been made
title.zh: 中东危机：鲁比奥希望美国“很快”与伊朗达成霍尔木兹协议

summary.en: US officials express hope for a swift deal with Iran regarding the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway through which Iraq alone exported over 30 million barrels of crude oil in one month.
summary.zh: 美国官员表示，希望很快与伊朗就具有战略意义的霍尔木兹海峡达成协议。数据显示，伊拉克仅在一个月内就通过这一关键水道出口了超过3000万桶原油。

body.en: US secretary of state comments come after treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said Washington could reach a deal ‘by tomorrow’ US and Qatar report progress on Iran ceasefire and reopening Hormuz strait Iran and Oman have made progress toward a deal to reopen the strait of Hormuz, a potential breakthrough that could help end the war in the Middle East, regional officials have said. Under the emerging agreement, ships would enter the Persian Gulf through an Iranian-controlled route and exit through a route controlled by Oman, with service fees charged for providing security and preserving the maritime environment, two regional officials told the Associated Press. Continue reading...
body.zh: 周二海事追踪公司 Kpler 的数据显示，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 表示，华盛顿可能在“明天之前”达成协议，伊拉克在一个月内通过战略性的霍尔木兹海峡出口了超过 3000 万桶原油。在中东战争导致重要水道运输受阻之前，伊拉克每天生产约 400 万桶石油，平均每月出口 1.05 亿桶石油，其中大部分通过霍尔木兹从巴士拉石油码头出口。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The ongoing diplomatic efforts to secure a deal in the Strait of Hormuz highlight the persistent human endeavor to find peaceful resolutions in complex geopolitical landscapes. This pursuit of peace, even when challenging, reflects the biblical call to live peaceably with all, striving for understanding and agreement wherever possible.
reflection.zh: 正在进行的关于霍尔木兹海峡协议的外交努力，凸显了人类在复杂地缘政治格局中寻求和平解决方案的持续努力。这种对和平的追求，即便充满挑战，也与圣经中呼吁与众人和睦相处的教导相符，提醒我们在可能的情况下，努力寻求理解和共识。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Chipotle removes jalapeños amid US salmonella outbreak investigation

summary.en: Chipotle has removed jalapeños from some of its restaurants as a precautionary measure. This action follows an investigation into a salmonella outbreak that has affected approximately 100 people, with the peppers identified as a potential source.
summary.zh: 奇波雷（Chipotle）餐厅已从部分门店下架墨西哥辣椒，以防万一。此前，一项针对沙门氏菌疫情的调查发现，这种辣椒可能是导致约100人患病的潜在原因。

body.en: Restaurant chain pulls peppers ‘out of an abundance of caution’ as salmonella outbreak sickens 100 people Chipotle said on Tuesday ⁠it had removed jalapeños from some of the chain’s restaurants after identifying ⁠the peppers as ⁠a ​potential ingredient tied to a salmonella outbreak, replacing them ⁠with supplies from different growers. The company said it ​began tracing ‌ingredients through its supply ‌chain after learning of a ‌potential outbreak and identified jalapeños from a common lot as a possible source. Continue reading...
body.zh: 沙门氏菌爆发导致 100 人患病，连锁餐厅出于谨慎考虑而下架了辣椒 Chipotle 周二表示，在确定辣椒是与沙门氏菌爆发有关的潜在成分后，该公司已从该连锁餐厅的部分餐厅中撤下了墨西哥辣椒，并用不同种植者的供应品取代了辣椒。该公司表示，在得知潜在的疫情爆发后，它开始通过供应链追踪成分，并确定来自普通批次的墨西哥辣椒可能是来源。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In situations involving public health, prudence and foresight are vital. Chipotle's decision to remove jalapeños “out of an abundance of caution” reflects a wise approach to potential danger, prioritizing safety even before definitive proof. This reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing harm and taking preventative steps to protect others.
reflection.zh: 在涉及公共健康的事件中，审慎和远见至关重要。奇波雷餐厅“出于高度谨慎”而下架墨西哥辣椒的决定，体现了对潜在危险的明智处理，即使在确凿证据出现之前也优先考虑安全。这提醒我们，预见危害并采取预防措施以保护他人是智慧之举。

title.en: Dinghy carrying 173 people capsizes in Channel after engine catches fire
title.zh: 载有173人的小艇在发动机起火后在英吉利海峡倾覆

summary.en: All passengers thought to have been taken to Boulogne after large air and sea rescue operation by France and UK A dinghy carrying 173 people has capsized after its engine caught fire as it attempted to cross the Channel from France. The people onboard were rescued from the water...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A dinghy carrying 173 people has capsized after its engine caught fire as it attempted to cross the Channel from France .

The people onboard were rescued from the water after a large air and sea operation was launched using UK border security and French vessels along with an RNLI boat.

According to French authorities there were initially 173 people onboard but five were rescued overnight in an earlier incident and taken back to Boulogne. The rest of the passengers said they wanted to continue their journey.

The dingy was carrying the highest number of people so far this year. A boat that arrived on 23 July was carrying 165 passengers.

A coastguard spokesperson said: “A vessel caught fire earlier this morning whilst in the French search and rescue region. UK vessels and a lifeboat are assisting.”

An RNLI spokesperson said Eastbourne’s all-weather lifeboat launched at 6am on Tuesday.

The Calais préfet said 40 firefighters and a specialised medical team were involved in the incident. Eleven people suffered minor injuries and three were taken to hospital in Boulogne.

On Monday, Reform UK proposed using the Royal Navy to return people to France or Belgium under a plan they called “operation fortress”. The party has described the scheme as a humanitarian response.

Last week, four people died on overcrowded boats trying to cross the Channel. Smugglers are using increasingly dangerous techniques in response to successive UK government clampdowns to stop crossings.

They are also launching boats from parts of the French coast that are farther away from the UK in the hope of evading French police interceptions. The boat on Tuesday reportedly left from Dieppe, about 70 miles (112km) from the UK compared with the Calais to Dover route of 27 miles.

The new prime minister, Andy Burnham , has promised to continue working to stop the crossings, although more than 2,000 people have crossed the Channel since he became prime minister. The government has put a number of deterrents in place to stop crossings, but desperate people continue to get into increasingly dangerous dinghies.

According to a statement issued by French authorities on Tuesday, the people in the boat initially refused an offer of assistance. “Given the structural fragility of the overcrowded boats, the decision was made not to force the migrants to board state rescue vessels, to avoid endangering their lives in the event of a shipwreck,” the statement read.
body.zh: 一艘载有 173 人的小艇在试图从法国横渡英吉利海峡时发动机起火，结果倾覆。 英国边境安全部门、法国船只以及 RNLI 船只发起大规模空中和海上行动，将船上人员从水中救出。 据法国当局称，船上最初有 173 人，但在早些时候的一次事故中，有 5 人连夜获救并被带回布洛涅。其余乘客表示他们想继续旅程。 这艘肮脏的飞机是今年迄今为止载客人数最多的。 7 月 23 日抵达的一艘船载有 165 名乘客。 海岸警卫队发言人表示：“今天早上，一艘船在法国搜救区起火。英国船只和一艘救生艇正在提供协助。” RNLI 发言人表示，伊斯特本的全天候救生艇于周二早上 6 点下水。 加莱省长表示，40 名消防员和一支专业医疗队参与了此次事件。十一人受轻伤，三人被送往布洛涅医院。 周一，英国改革组织提议利用皇家海军将人员送回法国或比利时，他们称之为“堡垒行动”。该党将该计划描述为人道主义响应。 上周，四人在试图穿越英吉利海峡的过度拥挤的船上死亡。走私者正在使用越来越危险的技术来应对英国政府连续不断的阻止过境的镇压。 他们还从距离英国较远的法国海岸部分地区下水，希望躲避法国警方的拦截。据报道，这艘船于周二从迪耶普出发，距离英国约 70 英里（112 公里），而加莱至多佛的路线为 27 英里。 新任总理安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 承诺将继续努力阻止越境行为，尽管自他就任总理以来已有 2,000 多人穿越英吉利海峡。政府已经采取了许多威慑措施来阻止过境，但绝望的人们继续乘坐越来越危险的小艇。 根据法国当局周二发表的声明，船上的人最初拒绝提供援助。声明中写道：“考虑到过度拥挤的船只结构脆弱，决定不强迫移民登上国家救援船，以免在发生海难时危及他们的生命。”

reflection.en: This story draws attention to creation care and environmental responsibility. Genesis 2:15 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with faithful stewardship of creation, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Video shows Russian drone chasing Ukrainian street vendor in 'human safari' attack
title.zh: 视频显示俄罗斯无人机“人类狩猎”式袭击，追逐乌克兰街头小贩

summary.en: Ukraine has condemned a video showing a Russian drone pursuing a civilian street vendor, labeling the incident a war crime.
summary.zh: 乌克兰谴责了一段显示俄罗斯无人机追逐一名平民街头小贩的视频，称该事件为战争罪。

body.en:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared a video on social media of a drone hunting down a man in southern Ukraine, saying it showed an instance of a Russian "safari" attack against civilians.

The video shows the drone pursuing a street vendor on a city street in the Kherson region. The man moves away from the drone hovering above, before it chases him as he runs around a white van. Eventually, the drone swoops down on him and explodes on impact.

The man escaped with multiple shrapnel wounds, concussion and trauma, a doctor said.

Sometimes called "human safari", the deployment of remotely-operated drones against civilians has often been used by Russians to terrify residents of front line areas in Ukraine.

"The world must see this," Zelensky wrote on Telegram. "It must see every piece of evidence that Russia has gone mad, and every fact that Russian soldiers are enjoying killings and tormenting people."

The video showed a "barbaric war crime", said Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.

The safaris were a "deliberate and systemic Russian strategy," Sybiha said. "The sadist operating this drone knows full well that he is targeting a civilian."

He added the attack was part of a deliberate Russian campaign to intimidate civilians and demanded international condemnation.

The Kherson regional governor later posted a video showing the man - identified as Yuriy, a 52-year-old street vegetable vendor - speaking from a hospital bed following the drone attack.

Yuriy said he and his wife had started to lay out crates of vegetables next to his van when he heard a distinctive buzzing sound overhead.

When his wife ran away, the drone turned to him instead. He held up some heads of garlic towards the drone's camera to show the operator that he was not trying to film it.

"It could see that I had tomatoes out, some cucumbers and eggplants laid out on the floor," Yuriy said. "It even ducked under the umbrella when I was running away round the other side."

BBC Verify geolocated the video to a market space beside a roundabout in the Tavriiskyi district in northern Kherson. It is not clear who filmed the attack, or how - but the earliest public copy BBC Verify found was shared by a pro-Ukrainian Instagram account on Tuesday morning.

"Safari" attacks have long been carried out by Russian troops in Kherson, which sits only a few miles from the front line.

A 2025 UN report said it had found Russian armed forces "recurrently killed and injured civilians" in the area by using drones to target them.

The videos filmed by the drones before they explode on to their targets are often posted online, allowing thousands to witness the last moments of the terrified victims.

body.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基在社交媒体上分享了一段无人机在乌克兰南部追捕一名男子的视频，称该视频展示了俄罗斯“狩猎”针对平民的袭击事件。 视频显示，无人机在赫尔松地区的一条城市街道上追赶一名街头小贩。该男子远离了盘旋在上方的无人机，随后无人机追赶他，他绕着一辆白色货车奔跑。最终，无人机向他俯冲并在撞击时爆炸。 一名医生称，这名男子逃脱后身受多处弹片伤、脑震荡和外伤。 有时被称为“人类狩猎”，俄罗斯人经常利用针对平民部署远程操作无人机来恐吓乌克兰前线地区的居民。 “世界必须看到这一点，”泽连斯基在 Telegram 上写道。 “它必须看到俄罗斯已经发疯的每一个证据，以及俄罗斯士兵享受杀戮和折磨人民的每一个事实。” 乌克兰外交部长安德里·西比哈 (Andrii Sybiha) 表示，该视频显示了“野蛮的战争罪行”。 西比哈说，这次狩猎是“俄罗斯深思熟虑的系统性战略”。 “操作这架无人机的虐待狂非常清楚他的目标是平民。” 他补充说，这次袭击是俄罗斯蓄意恐吓平民行动的一部分，并要求国际社会予以谴责。 赫尔松地区州长后来发布了一段视频，显示这名男子——52 岁的街头蔬菜摊贩尤里（Yuriy）——在无人机袭击后在医院病床上发表讲话。 尤里说，当他和妻子开始在货车旁边摆放蔬菜箱时，他听到头顶上有一种独特的嗡嗡声。 当他的妻子逃跑时，无人机转向了他。他向无人机的摄像头举起一些大蒜头，向操作员表明他并不是想拍摄它。 “它可以看到我把西红柿拿出来，一些黄瓜和茄子放在地板上，”尤里说。 “当我从另一边逃跑时，它甚至躲到了伞下。” BBC Verify 将该视频定位到赫尔松北部 Tavriiskyi 区环岛旁的一个市场空间。目前尚不清楚是谁拍摄了这次袭击，也不清楚如何拍摄的，但 BBC verify 发现的最早的公开副本是由亲乌克兰 Instagram 帐户于周二早上分享的。 俄罗斯军队长期以来一直在距前线仅几英里的赫尔松实施“狩猎”袭击。 联合国 2025 年的一份报告称，发现俄罗斯武装部队在该地区使用无人机瞄准平民，“经常造成平民伤亡”。 无人机在袭击目标之前拍摄的视频经常发布在网上，让数千人目睹了惊恐的受害者的最后时刻。 “发布平民伤亡的视频构成战争罪......

reflection.en: The disturbing video of a civilian being terrorized by a drone highlights a profound disregard for human life and dignity. Yahweh created humanity in His own image, bestowing inherent worth upon every individual, a truth that calls us to recognize and respect the sacred value of each person, even in conflict.
reflection.zh: 这段无人机恐吓平民的视频令人不安，它凸显了对人类生命和尊严的严重漠视。雅伟照着自己的形象创造了人类，赋予每个人固有的价值，这一真理呼唤我们在冲突中也要认识并尊重每个人的神圣价值。

title.en: More than 170 migrants rescued after boat catches fire in Channel
title.zh: 超过150名移民在英吉利海峡船只起火后获救

summary.en: French authorities reported that more than 150 migrants were rescued after their boat caught fire while attempting to cross the Channel to the UK.
summary.zh: 法国当局报告称，一艘载有移民的船只在试图穿越英吉利海峡前往英国时发动机起火，超过150名移民获救。

body.en:
More than 170 migrants have been rescued after the boat they were using to cross the Channel caught fire on Tuesday morning, as the UK government said "all will be returned" to France.

The boat was attempting to cross to the UK when its engine caught fire, according to the French maritime prefecture of the Channel and North Sea.

It had originally reported 157 migrants were rescued, but has since revised that figure up to 173. All have been taken to Boulogne-sur-Mer in France, with 11 people suffering from minor injuries.

French prosecutors have opened an investigation, and an Egyptian national has been taken into policy custody in connection with the incident.

Border Security Minister Anna Turley said the incident "shows the dangers of these illegal crossings and the ruthless gangs behind them".

Overnight "five people on board the vessel required rescue... the remaining people on board refused the assistance offered by the French patrol boats", the French maritime prefecture said.

"Determined to reach the United Kingdom, migrants crossing the Channel in small boats refused assistance offered by French emergency service, accepting it only in situations of extreme emergency," it said in a statement.

Because of the "structural fragility" of boats used to cross the Channel, it said they decided not to intervene further at that stage.

But this morning the engine caught fire and the "vessel's integrity deteriorated very rapidly".

Rescue boats went to the scene from France and the UK, including the RNLI Eastbourne lifeboat and the UK Border Force vessels BSC Contender and BSC Courageous.

The French maritime prefecture said the operation involved 40 firefighters, 13 police officers, seven interpreters, and a number of medical personnel.

It had previously reported that 157 migrants were rescued, but on Tuesday afternoon revised that figure up to 173.

On top of the initial five rescued, two French boats rescued 105 migrants and the British boats rescued 63. All of them were taken to Boulogne-sur-Mer for treatment.

A UK government spokesperson said the Border Security Command was alerted to an incident in the Channel this morning "concerning a migrant small boat in distress in French waters".

It said British vessels assisted in the operation, adding that so far there have been no fatalities reported.

They added that the incident "underlines the terrible dangers of small boat crossings".

"We continue to work relentlessly with the French and our partners overseas to prevent these perilous journeys," they said.

body.zh: 法国当局表示，周二上午，逾 150 名移民在穿越英吉利海峡时乘坐的船只起火，目前已获救。 据法国海峡和北海海事管辖区称，这艘船当时正试图穿越英国，但发动机起火。 据称，已有 157 人获救，并被送往滨海布洛涅的港口。目前还没有任何人受伤或死亡的报道。 就在一天前，英国首相安迪·伯纳姆(Andy Burnham)承诺，他的政府将“毫不留情”地限制乘小船抵达英国的人数。 法国海事局表示，夜间“船上有五人需要救援……船上其余人员拒绝了法国巡逻艇提供的援助”。 该组织在一份声明中表示：“乘坐小船穿越英吉利海峡的移民决心抵达英国，拒绝了法国紧急服务部门提供的援助，只有在极端紧急情况下才接受援助。” 由于用于穿越英吉利海峡的船只“结构脆弱”，声明称他们决定在该阶段不再进一步干预。 但今天早上，发动机着火了，“船舶的完整性迅速恶化”。 来自法国和英国的救援船已前往现场，其中包括 RNLI Eastbourne 救生艇以及英国边防部队的船只 BSC Contender 和 BSC Courageous。 他们全部被送往滨海布洛涅接受治疗，预计于周二当地时间 12:30（英国夏令时 11:30）抵达那里。 早些时候，英国海岸警卫队表示：“今天早上，一艘船在法国搜救区起火。英国船只和一艘救生艇正在提供协助。” 点击下面的问题 有多少人乘坐小船穿越英吉利海峡？ 2026年1月1日至8月1日期间，共有14,526人从法国乘小船穿越英吉利海峡。这比去年同期下降了 43%。 自2020年以来，这些过境点已成为被发现非法进入英国的最常见方式。 几乎所有乘小船抵达的人都申请庇护。根据国际法，这意味着他们在考虑庇护申请期间可以留在该国。 2025年4月至2026年3月期间，小船抵达的庇护申请占42%。 2025年8月2日至2026年8月1日抵达英国的船只平均载有67人。自 2021 年以来，这一数字增加了一倍多。 专家表示，船只过度拥挤使得过境的风险更大。据联合国 (UN) 称，2024 年至少有 84 人在试图穿越英吉利海峡时死亡。 从小船过境规模来看，这些到达的人数约为小船规模的 5%...

Yahweh is often described as our ultimate refuge, and we are called to reflect...

title.en: Oil prices fall on hopes Strait of Hormuz could reopen
title.zh: 油价下跌，因霍尔木兹海峡有望重开

summary.en: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced progress in talks aimed at allowing shipments to resume through the Strait of Hormuz, leading to a fall in oil prices.
summary.zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥和财政部长斯科特·贝森特均宣布，旨在允许船只恢复通过霍尔木兹海峡的谈判取得了进展，导致油价下跌。

body.en:
Oil prices fell to a three-week low on Tuesday as senior US officials raised hopes of a deal with Iran to reopen the key Strait of Hormuz waterway.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent both announced talks had progressed to allow shipments to potentially resume as soon as this week.

The cost of a barrel of Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil prices, fell by almost 5% to under $80 (£60) on the news of supply disruptions potentially being eased.

But the failure of previous negotiations in recent months to de-escalate the conflict between the US and Iran has led to a volatile oil market, with drivers ultimately being hit by higher fuel prices at the pumps.

On Tuesday, along with the drop in Brent crude, US West Texas Intermediate prices were down more than 5%, to $76 a barrel. Both contracts dropped to their lowest levels since 13 July.

Rubio said there had been progress made in discussions on getting more ships through the Strait with Iran and Oman.

"There's been progress made in those talks, but not finality yet. We're hoping that will happen very shortly," he told reporters at the State Department.

Bessent said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be agreed as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday.

There was a "chance we may have a deal today or tomorrow to open the strait and move towards a more normalized position in this conflict," he told CNBC.

"It would be freedom of movement," he added, when asked whether Iran would be allowed to charge for ships passing through.

While senior figures in the US government have announced talks have been progressing, no details of what a potential deal may look like have been released.

Iran has said it is not negotiating with the US - and has no plans to do so - and is instead talking to Oman.

A spokesman for Iran's foreign ministry said that talks with Oman, a mediator in negotiations, on a new mechanism for vessels going through the Strait, had been positive.

Qatar, which is a key mediator between Washington and Tehran, said it was continuing efforts with other mediators to try to achieve a diplomatic resolution to the war, but admitted no direct talks were currently planned.

The Strait of Hormuz has been a central point in negotiations between the US and Iran. Before the conflict began in late February, the waterway handled about one-fifth of global daily oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.

"Investors are acutely aware of how many times we've already been at this point in the war and how fragile the process of securing lasting agreements can be," said Danni Hewson, head of financial analysis at AJ Bell.

reflection.en: The news of diplomatic progress to reopen a vital shipping lane reminds us of the quiet, persistent work of peacemaking. When leaders engage in dialogue to resolve tensions and restore stability, they embody the spirit of those whom Yahweh blesses for bringing peace. Such efforts, even in complex geopolitical situations, can bring tangible relief and hope.
reflection.zh: 恢复重要航运通道的外交进展提醒我们，缔造和平的工作是安静而持久的。当领导人通过对话解决紧张局势并恢复稳定时，他们体现了那些因带来和平而蒙雅伟赐福之人的精神。即使在复杂的地缘政治局势中，这样的努力也能带来切实的缓解和希望。

title.en: Watch: Evacuations as Guatemala volcano erupts
title.zh: 观看：危地马拉火山喷发时的疏散

summary.en: The Fuego volcano is located near Escuintla, Chimaltenango, and Sacatepéquez.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Fuego volcano, located between the Escuintla, Chimaltenango, and Sacatepéquez regions, registered an increase in its activity on Monday, prompting Guatemalan authorities to declare an "orange alert" - the second highest emergency.

Around 400 people were evacuated from communities near the volcano and taken to temporary shelters in Alotenango and Escuintla city. Schools close to the volcano were closed due to the risk of ash fall and further volcanic activity.

Emergency services urged residents to leave their homes for their safety. In 2018, a violent eruption of the Fuego volcano left hundreds dead .

Fuego is just 16km (10 miles) west of Antigua, a city popular with tourists, who travel to the Unesco World Heritage Site to admire its colonial-era architecture. The active stratovolcano has also become popular with hikers .

title.en: EU commends Spain's 'swift response' to Ceuta migrant crisis
title.zh: 欧盟赞扬西班牙对休达移民危机的“迅速反应”

summary.en: About 70,000 of the 72,000 people who came to Ceuta illegally last week have been returned to Morocco, Spain says.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The European Union has praised Spain's "swift response" to the migrant crisis in Ceuta, following a meeting of the bloc's interior ministers on Tuesday.

Around 72,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory in North Africa between 30 and 31 July, Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said. He added that an estimated 70,000 have since been returned to Morocco.

At least 75 people died on the Spanish side of the border, while 11 deaths were reported in Morocco.

Tuesday's meeting was called after several EU members expressed concern over Spain's handling of the crisis, with Italy describing images from Ceuta as "shocking" and suspending its Schengen agreement with Spain.

Irish Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan, who chaired Tuesday's meeting, said the EU stood in solidarity with Spain and that migration required "a united European response".

The meeting had been expected to draw some tension, following earlier criticism of Spain from some EU nations.

On Thursday, Italy's right-wing Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said such "uncontrolled immigration" was a security threat to Europe.

Italy suspended its Schengen zone agreement with Spain on free movement on Friday, but since the two countries do not share a land border, this would only apply, effectively, to flights - which appears simply to mean extra checks for passengers.

The Schengen agreement eliminates border checks and now encompasses more than 450 million people and 29 countries in Europe.

Finland and Denmark backed Italy's move, while Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš urged a temporary suspension of Spain's Schengen membership.

Italy, along with Denmark and 20 other nations, later sent a letter expressing their concern over the Ceuta migrant crisis.

In response, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he had "serious concerns" about some European governments and pointed out that Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area.

While most had shown "support and solidarity", he said other European governments had chosen to attack Spain, "driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest".

Speaking after the meeting on Tuesday, Grande-Marlaska said the Schengen zone had not been compromised and that he hoped Italy would lift any added controls "as soon as possible".

Denmark's immigration minister Morten Bødskov said he was "very satisfied" with Spain's quick response, but added that the incident showed "it is absolutely crucial that we have control over the EU's borders".

Speaking afterwards, EU commissioner Magnus Brunner said the incident had been a "test" of European resilience and border security - which he said it had successfully "passed".

title.en: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
title.zh: 南苏丹：气候变化如何导致有毒水

summary.en: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

The village of Bentiu has seen it all: Located in the north of South Sudan near the border with Sudan , the capital of Unity State used to have a population of merely several thousand people.

But war, violence and other crisis have resulted in an additional 140,000 displaced persons seeking shelter there since 2013, resulting in the establishment of a massive camp for internally displaced persons (IDPs).

Several UN bodies including the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the  UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR ) and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) are active on the ground, running what is known as the Protection of Civilians (POC) camp, which by now feels more like a permanent structure.

At a makeshift pier, children are seen playing, countless canoes bring in fish to feed scores of people at the camp, where food insecurity remains a chief concern.

Immediately, each day's yield is separated into two categories: One stock with fresh, healthy fish, and another for those believed to be contaminated. 

Simon Gatkuoth, a camp resident in his early forties, lifts a fish from a wheelbarrow, explaining that fish that are caught near the oil fields are contaminated: "When we cook them, the soup sometimes smells like penicillin," he says.

"But there is no option. We have to eat. We cannot stop eating because there is no alternative."

Viewed from the sky, the POC Camp resembles an artificial island in the midst of a region that has been transformed into what appears to be a gigantic lake. 

Here, the largely nomadic communities of South Sudan's Unity State have long adapted their lives to the seasonal floods that shape life in what is one of the world's largest wetlands known as the Sudd.

But in 2021, and unprecedented deluge of floods linked to climate change submerged farmland across the region, destroying livelihoods and killing thousands of cattle.

title.en: What does Zambia's opposition stand without Edgar Lungu?
title.zh: 如果没有埃德加·伦古，赞比亚的反对派会怎样？

summary.en: The death of former President Edgar Lungu reshaped opposition politics in Zambia ahead of the August 13 general election. Analysts say the vote will test whether his legacy can keep opposition supporters united.

body.en:
The death of former President Edgar Lungu reshaped opposition politics in Zambia ahead of the August 13 general election. Analysts say the vote will test whether his legacy can keep opposition supporters united.

Zambia 's opposition is entering the 2026 general election without Edgar Lungu, the politician who for years united its biggest parties and inspired much of its support. Lungu, the country's former president, died in South Africa on June 5, 2025 .

Opposition parties have since been competing to inherit his political legacy while trying to convince voters they remain a credible alternative to incumbent Hakainde Hichilema's ruling United Party for National Development (UPND).

Lungu had led the now dismantled Patriotic Front (PF) party, a faction of which became part of Zambia's overall opposition Tonse Alliance in 2024. The former president had also intitially been fronted as the coalition's 2026 presidential candidate.

Political analyst Neo Simutanyi says Lungu's absence exposes an unresolved leadership question within the opposition coalition.

"He had a Plan B. He intended to back someone who would carry forward his political project, but he never had the opportunity to announce that person before he died," Simutanyi told DW.

Competing claims emerged over who should lead the Tonse Alliance emerged after Lungu's death. The coalition, now rebranded as the Tonse Pamodzi Alliance, has endorsed Brian Mundubile as its 2026 presidential candidate. He and Lungu were PF allies, while his running mate, Makebi Zulu, was Lungu's lawyer. Mundubile is widely seen as Hichilema's top challenger.

Simutanyi believes Lungu's influence nevertheless remains significant. "It is effectively a PF campaign without the PF label," he said, adding that several candidates are appealing to the same support base by presenting themselves as heirs to Lungu's legacy.

"The Edgar Lungu factor is still at play because candidates are campaigning on his legacy and many of the areas where he enjoyed strong support remain politically competitive."

Lungu's influence remains particularly visible on the Copperbelt, Zambia's mining heartland  and one of the country's most competitive electoral battlegrounds.

"Edgar Lungu's absence has left a big vacuum in the opposition, especially in the Patriotic Front. He was the one holding the party together," said Agness Tembo, a young leader from the Copperbelt.

She warned that a fragmented opposition could weaken Zambia's competitive multiparty democracy. But not all voters believe personalities will decide the election.

title.en: Is Bangladesh backtracking on post-Hasina reforms?
title.zh: 孟加拉国是否会在哈西娜后的改革中倒退？

summary.en: Two years after a student-led uprising toppled PM Sheikh Hasina, critics say Bangladesh's reform momentum is fading as political divisions deepen and key changes stall.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two years after a student-led uprising toppled PM Sheikh Hasina, critics say Bangladesh's reform momentum is fading as political divisions deepen and key changes stall.

Just two years after a student-led uprising ended the nearly 16-year rule of Sheikh Hasina , many fear Bangladesh is slipping backward.

With Hasina, now in exile in India , planning a return in December and critics accusing the current government of failing to deliver on its promises, the country's political future is once again in doubt.

"At the end of the day, we did not see the elimination of discrimination, the creation of an inclusive society, or the new political order that was promised," Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan, a professor of international relations at Dhaka University, told DW.

"It seems we are forgetting the very reasons behind the uprising of last July, especially those who came to power."

The protest movement began in 2018 over a controversial quota system for government jobs. In 2024, a court-backed move to reinstate parts of the system sparked fresh demonstrations that grew into a wider anti-government uprising .

In August 2024, after more than 1,000 people were killed in the unrest , then Prime Minister Hasina fled to India .

Bangladesh's interim government , which was led by Nobel Peace Prize winner Muhammad Yunus and backed by the military and key figures from the uprising, facilitated the signing of a reform roadmap. It was named the "July Charter" after the month when the uprising that toppled Hasina began. 

In a February 2026 referendum, around 70% of voters approved the charter, which proposed term limits for prime ministers, the creation of an upper house of parliament, stronger presidential powers and greater judicial independence.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won a decisive majority in a general election that took place alongside the referendum .

Critics say the BNP has since failed to implement several pre-election reform commitments.

Ali Riaz, who led the interim government's Constitution Reform Commission, said there had been "time-bound commitments," including the creation of a constitutional reform council and steps to implement reforms within 180 working days.

The interim government introduced 133 ordinances as part of its reform agenda, but after the BNP came to power, it refused to adopt 20 of them — including measures concerning the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), the Anti-Corruption Commission, enforced disappearances and referendums.

The BNP argues that constitutional and institutional changes should be enacted through proper legislative procedures in Parliament.

title.en: Spain clashes with EU countries in heated talks over migration fallout

summary.en: An estimated 60,000 people rushed into Spain's North African territory, causing major concerns throughout the European Union.
summary.zh: 估计有六万人涌入西班牙的北非领土，引发了整个欧盟的重大关切。

body.en:
Spain's interior minister headed into a tense face-off with EU counterparts on Tuesday, as the bloc sought to draw lessons from an influx of migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in hastily arranged video talks.

The unprecedented sight of an estimated 60,000 people streaming into Ceuta from Morocco — dozens died in the attempt and almost all have since left — exposed the fault lines on migration among EU nations.

Since images first emerged of the mass arrivals, most of whom swam around a barrier separating the enclave from Morocco, the Spanish government has found itself pitted against many of its EU partners.

The bloc's interior ministers dialled in for a videoconference that could provide a chance to look for common ground — but looked equally likely to set the stage for a showdown.

While Spain moved swiftly to send migrants back from Ceuta — where it said an estimated 2,500 remained as of Monday — the government of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez backs a more open approach to migration than most of its EU counterparts.

Countries pushing a harder line are led most vocally by Italy — whose Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has attacked Madrid's stance, and specifically a recent push to grant legal status to undocumented migrants already in the country.

Both Italy and Denmark last week advocated suspending Spain from the Schengen free-travel area over the Ceuta crisis — a notion firmly rejected by Madrid, and which in any case is legally impossible under EU rules.

In a letter to the heads of the EU's institutions Saturday, Sanchez accused fellow EU countries of having "selfish" attitudes and called for emergency talks to work on a "common response" to such incidents.

Within hours, 22 countries led by Italy, Denmark, Germany and Hungary sent a counter-letter also demanding urgent talks, but with a different goal: to continue pressing their tough stance on immigration.

In a taste of what to expect, preparatory talks among the bloc's EU ambassadors on Monday saw Spain's envoy voice "frustration" with a perceived lack of support from fellow capitals, one EU diplomat told the Agence-France Presse (AFP) news agency.

Conversely — while all assured Madrid of their "solidarity" — some member states "are asking themselves if recent policies adopted by Spain have not sent the signal that the doors are open", added the diplomat.

The EU has significantly tightened its migration rules in recent months, including by allowing member states to send failed asylum seekers to so-called "return hubs" located outside the bloc's borders.

body.en:
Once seen as a leading opposition figure, Pahlavi now faces questions about his political relevance in Western capitals and inside Iran.

An investigation by Reuters news agency into Reza Pahlavi , the son of the last shah of Iran , has raised a question: has Iran's most prominent opposition figure abroad lost credibility and influence among Western policymakers and Iranians?

Reuters reported in July that Pahlavi's candidacy had "sputtered" after appearing to reach its high point earlier this year.

Although he has repeatedly declared his readiness to lead Iran through a transitional period, senior US officials have publicly distanced themselves from the prospect of a US-backed effort to bring Pahlavi to power.

The Reuters report notes that critics accuse Pahlavi of relying too heavily on foreign military intervention and failing to build a lasting political coalition.

During periods of heightened tensions, Pahlavi welcomed international pressure on the Islamic Republic.

In January 2026, he told Iranians that the international community had entered the stage of action and echoed US President Donald Trump's message that help was "on its way."

"Great nation of Iran, the eyes of the world are upon you. Take to the streets, and as a united front, shout your demands," Pahlavi wrote on X. 

After the military conflict  failed to bring about the collapse of the Iranian government and criticism intensified over the consequences of war, Pahlavi said that "the final victory will still be forged by our hands" and that it was the Iranian people who would "finish the job."

The main responsibility, he said, remained with the Iranian people themselves. Some critics argued that this emphasis on the role of the Iranian people marked a retreat from his earlier messaging about international help.

"A serious alternative would need the capacity to gain and manage power, influence existing power structures and offer a realistic prospect of structural political change," Najafi said. "Western governments have never considered Pahlavi to have met these criteria."

Najafi distinguishes between Europe and the United States. "European governments primarily approach Iran from the perspective of stability," he said, pointing to migration, geopolitical and security concerns, and the containment of radicalism and terrorism.

body.en:
Japan needs to boost its military with a "sense of urgency and crisis", its defence minister said on Tuesday, as a new government assessment reiterated growing risks from China, North Korea, and Russia.

Japan is already beefing up military spending and security cooperation in Asia, deploying missile launchers to outer islands, moving to acquire "counter-strike" capabilities, and easing rules on weapons exports.

But Shinjiro Koizumi said in a preface to the annual defence white paper that it was "imperative that Japan further reinforce and transform its defense capabilities with a stronger sense of urgency and crisis than ever before".

In the Asia-Pacific "not only are China and North Korea further strengthening their military capabilities, China-Russia and Russia-North Korea are also reinforcing their cooperation", he added.

The new white paper said China was "intensifying its activities" in the region around Japan, "extending beyond the so-called first island chain to the second island chain".

Japan decided in April to lift its self-imposed ban on weapons exports, but the white paper highlighted problems in the country's production base that could jeopardise procurement and innovation.

Koizumi also said that he and US counterpart Pete Hegseth had "exchanged candid views" on the "unwavering" US-Japan alliance, while also increasing security cooperation with the Philippines, Australia, and South Korea to realise a "a Free and Open Indo-Pacific".

"As the security environment becomes increasingly and rapidly severe, what is required now is to strengthen resilience against crises all across the entire Indo-Pacific region," Koizumi said.

"In order to do so Japan will build and expand multilayered networks among allies and like-minded countries, and enhance interconnectivity with like-minded countries and others in every area."

body.en:
Photographs of Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi meeting with an aid agency have been released, a visit her son described as "extremely meaningful".

It is the first independent confirmation of her condition in years as uncertainty over the health and well-being of the 81-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner continued to grow.

Suu Kyi has been detained since February 2021, when Myanmar's military ousted her elected civilian government in a dawn coup , plunging the impoverished Southeast Asian nation into turmoil.

The whereabouts of the former head of Myanmar's pro-Democracy party, who has a large global following, have remained largely unknown since then.

Suu Kyi's son, Kim Aris, told the Reuters news agency that the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) had not been allowed to have a physician examine his mother, but said she appeared to be in good health and good spirits.

Mon Zin, an Australian-based lawyer who fled Myanmar in the 1990s with her family, told SBS News the photos offer "relief" to her supporters.

Zin is the daughter of democracy activists who fled Myanmar for Australia in 1996, where she was enrolled in Year 10.

Three decades on, she is now a lawyer and regularly contributes to analysis pieces for geopolitical publications.

She told SBS News that Suu Kyi is an "admired figure" across Asia for her decades of opposing despotism in Myanmar.

"We have always admired Aung San Suu Kyi's resilience and strength. For the people of Myanmar and many in the resistance movement, when they saw the photograph, it brought them genuine relief," she said.

One of four photographs released by the Myanmar government showed Suu Kyi in traditional Burmese dress, standing unaided and shaking hands with an ICRC representative.

Another showed the pair seated in a sparsely furnished, wood-panelled room with only two chairs and a desk.

"Timing is everything. Those who control when information is released often shape how it is interpreted and, in doing so, influence the narrative," she said.

"The junta chose to publicise a carefully managed humanitarian meeting with the ICRC, projecting humanitarian optics while continuing to deny political access to ASEAN, foreign diplomats and even her own family," Zin said.

"While many of us were relieved to see Aung San Suu Kyi alive, it is equally important to ask: Why was this information released at this particular moment?"

title.en: Nauru has become Naoero, the latest nation to join a growing cultural trend
title.zh: 瑙鲁更名为瑙埃罗，加入日益增长的文化趋势

summary.en: The island nation of Nauru has officially reverted to its original name, the Republic of Naoero, reflecting a broader global trend of nations reclaiming their indigenous cultural identities.
summary.zh: 瑙鲁岛国已正式恢复其原名瑙埃罗共和国，这反映了全球范围内各国重新认同其本土文化身份的趋势。

body.en:
The Pacific island nation of Nauru has officially changed its name to the Republic of Naoero, reverting to its traditional designation in a move it said was aimed at strengthening national identity and cultural heritage.

Nauru's parliament passed a constitutional amendment in May to rename the country, initially planning a national referendum. However, President David Adeang said in a social media post last week that the referendum plans have been dropped.

"The decision not to pursue a referendum was reached after thoughtful deliberation that Naoero is not a new name seeking acceptance by the people," Adeang said.

"It is already the identity of the people, is on the national coat of arms, and spoken in the community; and importantly is allowed by the constitution."

The abbreviated name will be "Naoero", while citizens will be referred to as "dei-Naoero".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

European colonisers changed the country's name to Nauru after finding it difficult to pronounce the island's native name Naoero.

The nation is the world's third-smallest after Vatican City and Monaco, with a population of about 12,000.

Adeang said the decision was not about politics but about identity, heritage, and "preserving the legacy of our ancestors and strengthening the future of our children".

The government has formally notified international organisations and countries of the change, with the transition process already underway.

Over the last 50 years, a trend of smaller nations asserting their independence from old colonial empires has given rise to a growing cultural trend — the national name change.

For many nations like Naoero, the desire to revert to its original, pre-colonial name is about cementing a sense of national identity or pride.

Timor-Leste adopted its current name — a Portuguese tautology in which both words mean "East" — in 2002. It was previously known as Timor Timur — its Indonesian name that, funnily enough, also meant "East East" — from 1975 until independence.

Tuvalu and Kiribati took back their names in 1978 and 1979 respectively, doing away with colonial names the Ellice Islands and Gilbert Islands.

Vanuatu followed suit in 1980, retiring the name New Hebrides after becoming independent.

Overseas, Türkiye was among the most recent major nations to change its name.

Its campaign for a name change started in 2021 when Turkish president Recep Erdoğan began asking various international bodies to observe the traditional spelling and pronunciation.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

"A great degree [of its success] is due to the talent, infrastructure and the resources that were poured into building this...
body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

title.en: Aboriginal police officers in the NT underpaid and racially abused, a new class action alleges
title.zh: 一项新的集体诉讼称，北领地的原住民警察工资过低并受到种族虐待

summary.en: Aboriginal community police officers in the NT Police Force allege they were subject to racial discrimination while serving.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name of an Indigenous person who has passed away.

When former AFL player for Essendon, Shawn Lewfatt, signed up as an Aboriginal Community Police Officer in Darwin in 1998, he was excited by the chance to work with his own people "for the better".

Now, he says, he would "never encourage" his adult children to join the Northern Territory Police Force (NTPF).

"My aim is that hopefully one day I can turn to young people and encourage them to join," he told SBS News.

Lewfatt is part of a landmark class action filed in the Federal Court against the NTPF seeking compensation for allegations of racial discrimination and racial vilification while serving as Aboriginal Community Police Officers (ACPOS) going back almost three decades.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Our clients allege they were underpaid, provided fewer opportunities for career advancement and subjected to persistent racist conduct while serving communities across the NT," Seb O'Meara of Gordon Legal, who is representing the ACPOs in the class action, told SBS News.

The class action, run on behalf of all present and former Aboriginal police officers in the NT Police, seeks to speed up reform following the 2019 police shooting of Kumanjayi Walker and the subsequent inquest, which shone the spotlight on systemic racism within the NT Police Force.

A spokesperson for the NTPF told SBS News they were aware of ongoing legal proceedings, and it would be inappropriate to comment further.

Despite growing up in Darwin, Lewfatt told SBS News that when he walked through the doors of the police station, he felt like a "foreigner in my hometown".

"I felt immediately weird in the way they would speak about Aboriginal people, and it became clear to me that it was the norm."

Lewfett, who remains on the Force on leave, alleged he witnessed "unlawful assaults on Indigenous people", including one incident involving a non-Aboriginal police officer urinating into a wine cask belonging to an Aboriginal member of the public who had stashed it in a public toilet.

Lewfatt said that racism in the force is embedded in the culture, rather than in individuals.

"It's the systematic racism where there are a lot of good people who may not be racist but do not call out racism either when they come across it."

title.en: 'Free-range' eggs could face existential threat amid bird flu warning
title.zh: 禽流感警告下，‘散养’鸡蛋或面临生存威胁

summary.en: Experts are warning that the bird flu threat could end free-range egg farming, as confining birds to barns is now considered necessary for their welfare.
summary.zh: 专家警告称，禽流感威胁可能终结散养鸡蛋养殖，因为现在将禽鸟限制在禽舍内被认为是保障其福利的必要措施。

body.en:
The egg industry has so far remained unaffected by the H5N1 avian influenza (bird flu) outbreak; however, precautionary measures to limit the spread of the virus could drastically reduce free-range egg production.

The recent H5N1 outbreak in South Australia has sparked widespread concern for the health and safety of not only the wild bird population but also commercial farming.

Australian Eggs managing director Rowan McMonnies said the industry is "facing up to a riskier operating environment for the foreseeable future".

"Transmission between Australian wildlife indicates H5 avian influenza is established and is here to stay in the medium term," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

McMonnies said whilst eradication "seems unlikely", the industry has been preparing for an outbreak of this type for several years.

"Important actions are being taken to address the risks. Strict biosecurity is being maintained with enhanced measures to deter wild birds and limit crossover into egg farms," he said.

"The industry has also worked closely with authorities to improve response processes based on overseas learnings so that where farms are impacted, they can bounce back faster, limiting any impact on egg supply."

Since 2018, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has enforced the standard that for an egg product to be considered free range it must be laid by hens that have meaningful and regular access to outdoor range during daylight, are able to roam and forage in a stocking density of 10,000 hens or less per hectare, and that the density be displayed on produced products.

However, as of July, the ACCC confirmed it won’t take enforcement action for breaches of free-range egg labelling standards due to farms choosing to house birds inside for biosecurity reasons.

Limiting free-range environments is a biosecurity measure many chicken farms are using.

"The advice is to confine birds to sheds," microbiologist and food safety expert Associate Professor Julian Cox told SBS News.

"Birds of free-ranging pick up the virus and interact — potentially spreading it to noncommercial species .... or wild birds in the vicinity could bring it into commercial poultry that are free-ranging," he explained.

Cox said it’s a measure anyone who owns and cares for poultry should consider.

"If you've got some kind of coop, lock them in the coop. It’s for their own good."

Cox, who also serves as the scientific director of the Food Safety Information Council, said if an outbreak does occur in a commercial facility, there are processes that would be implemented to restrict its impact.

title.en: Why some Australians could go uncounted this Census
title.zh: 为什么一些澳大利亚人可能在人口普查中被漏算

summary.en: Census field officers in Australia are actively working to ensure that vulnerable populations, who might otherwise be overlooked, are accurately counted in the national census.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的人口普查员正积极工作，以确保那些可能被忽视的弱势群体能够被准确地纳入全国人口普查。

body.en:
As day turns to dusk at Waterloo Green park in Sydney's inner south, a crowd gathers to access free haircuts, optometry and dental check-up services.

There are snags on the barbecue and one attendant tells SBS News the Homelessness Week event — dubbed Refresh, Recharge & Shine — is "fantastic".

"There should be more things like this for people in need," Marie said while assisting at the event.

NSW housing and homelessness minister Rose Jackson, who was also there on 3 August, told SBS News she believes "people don't like to think about what it's like to be homeless" but that it was important to draw the issue into the national conversation.

"Knowing how many people are living homeless, where they are, what their demographic is, their age, their gender — that's critical information for the government."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Jackson said data collected during the Census of Population and Housing on 11 August will be "crucial" for allocating resources and services to people experiencing homelessness.

"I think the ABS [Australian Bureau of Statistics] has done a really good job lifting its level of engagement. I think maybe in the past it wasn't something that was recognised as a priority," Jackson said.

"The Census was built around [dropping] a form into people's letterbox — and for people that don't have letterboxes, where do you start?"

Sharon Callister, CEO of Mission Australia, has been working alongside Census field officers to help people experiencing housing insecurity complete the Census.

"There are rough sleepers in Sydney, and many of them are in known rough sleeping spots. Our support services staff go out there. There are also field offices coming from the Census office," she told SBS News.

She said people in temporary dwellings like boarding houses or hostels can access paper Census forms from accommodation staff.

Callister said it can be difficult to capture "hidden homeless" populations. That includes people sleeping in a car or tent, or couch surfing with friends, family or acquaintances without a secure lease.

"We're at a critical point in Australia. The last Census, there were [more than] 122,000 people homeless. We know from our services today that that number is going to be higher this year."

If someone is experiencing homelessness , the ABS advises people to write "NONE" in response to the question about where they usually live. Online, this question can be answered by selecting the "Elsewhere in Australia" option, then manually entering "NONE" in the suburb and locality boxes.

title.en: The growing constituency reshaping Australian politics
title.zh: 日益壮大的选民群体正在重塑澳大利亚政治

summary.en: A new study reveals that home ownership significantly impacts how Australians vote, indicating its growing influence on the nation's political landscape.
summary.zh: 一项新研究发现，房屋所有权影响澳大利亚人的投票方式，这表明它对该国政治格局的影响日益增长。

body.en:
The ongoing housing crisis is having severe repercussions on individuals and families in Australia. It has limited young people’s ability to move out, increased the rate of involuntary lifelong renting, and pushed vulnerable populations into homelessness.

These are not the only changes that flow as a result of housing unaffordability. Our new research demonstrates it’s also reshaping how people vote.

A longstanding body of academic work links individuals’ assets to their political and ideological beliefs, including the parties they vote for.

This literature shows people with more valuable assets are more likely to hold right-leaning political beliefs. They are also more likely to support conservative parties that favour the status quo over efforts to redistribute money and wealth more equitably throughout a society.

For the average person, the family home is the most valuable asset they will ever own. However, surprisingly few studies have considered the influence of home ownership on voting preferences. Australia represents an interesting case study for two key reasons.

First, Australian major political parties differ in their electoral positions regarding housing policy. In particular, the Coalition of the Liberal and National parties has historically favoured homeowners through — for example — negative gearing and tax discounts. In contrast, since the 2010s, the Australian Greens and the Labor Party have progressively adopted more pro-renter stances.

Second, Australia’s trend towards housing unaffordability is particularly pronounced by international standards. This is reflected in increased home and rental prices, reduced homeownership rates and increased property-ownership concentration. This situation creates a greater divide in the economic interests of renters and homeowners, potentially shifting (or entrenching) party preferences.

Our new study explored how housing tenure relates to voting behaviour in Australia. We also wanted to know whether the relationship has become stronger over time.

We analysed survey data from more than 19,000 people participating in ten iterations of the Australian Election Study between 1996 and 2022. The Australian Electoral Study interviews people shortly after each national election, collecting information on their demographic traits, economic position and sociopolitical attitudes.

We analysed these survey data to examine associations between individuals’ self-reported housing tenure and the party they voted for in the last election. We also kept other relevant factors constant, such as age, income, area of residence...

title.en: 'Unfounded and premature': Why experts say parents shouldn't panic about screen time
title.zh: “毫无根据且为时过早”：为什么专家说父母不应该对屏幕时间感到恐慌

summary.en: New international research is challenging fears about a link between children's screen time and developmental delay.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Concerns about children and screen use may be overblown, new research suggests, with experts saying worries about an 'iPad baby' generation may be "premature".

A new international study, based on data from over 3,000 children, found no link between screen use duration and developmental difficulties at ages five or 10.

Researchers in the UK spoke with the families of children back in 2009 and 2010 and followed their development for the subsequent 10 years.

Over that time, there has been some criticism and debate about the role of technology in parenting, and whether young people born in the 21st century will be a screen-addicted generation.

The iPad was released in Australia in 2010, and a child growing up around this time is sometimes referred to as an 'iPad baby'.

While the findings are limited by self-reported survey data, Australian experts say the results counter popular messaging about parenting and technology.

"Fear from parents around screen time is unfounded and premature," Associate Professor David Armstrong from the School of Education at La Trobe University told SBS News.

"It's really a mixed bag over whether there are any adverse effects on kids' development, and it's good to note that there are some advantages of devices for social development."

He described the findings as "robust and methodical", saying they contribute to an emerging body of research calling not for less screen time, but for better use of it.

But Professor Andrew Whitehouse, an autism researcher at The Kids Research Institute Australia, said the findings should be taken with a grain of salt, as young children in 2026 have access to more smart devices than in 2009.

"The saturation of childhood by these devices came in the years afterwards," he said in a statement.

"This means that across early childhood, the children had almost no exposure to the ubiquity of smart devices as now exists."

As content increasingly targets children and is designed to maximise viewing time, experts say the best tools parents have are managing content and ensuring quality time away from screens.

Screen time is not inherently harmful said Adam Guastella, a clinical psychologist who works with Sydney Children's Hospital at Westmead and the University of Sydney.

Rather, the effects on a child's physical, cognitive and social development come down to content.

"If you're doing the same thing repetitively over and over and over again, in terms of cognitive development, that's not going to be good. Particularly if what you're practising doesn't have any functional significance," he told SBS News.
